subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Light Roast: Origin Forward
description: A quick, practical guide to Light Roast: Origin Forward.

hook.text: Light roasts are pulled at or shortly after first crack. They preserve the bean's origin character above all else.

buildup.text: Flavors lean toward fruit, floral, citrus, and tea-like notes. Acidity is high. Body is lighter. Color is cinnamon to tan.

discovery.text: Light roasting requires exceptional green coffee—there's nowhere for defects to hide when the roast barely masks anything.

twist.text: Many people find light roasts too acidic or 'sour' if they're used to dark roast. It's an acquired preference.

climax.text: The specialty coffee movement champions light roasts. They let terroir and processing speak louder than the roaster's hand.

punchline.text: Light roast: the bean talks. The roaster listens.

quiz.question: Why does light roasting require high-quality green coffee?
options: There's nowhere for defects to hide when the roast barely masks anything

details.summary: Light roasts are pulled shortly after first crack, preserving the bean's natural acidity, fruit notes, and floral aromas. They showcase the terroir and processing method more than the roast itself. Specialty coffee culture prizes light roasts for their transparency.
details.whyItMatters: Light roasts reveal a coffee's origin story, making them the preferred style for evaluating quality and distinguishing between regions and farms.
takeaways: Light roasts preserve acidity, fruit, and floral notes
They are stopped shortly after first crack begins
Origin character is more apparent than roast character

faq.question: Do light roasts have more caffeine than dark roasts?
faq.answer: The difference is minimal. Caffeine is remarkably heat-stable, so roast level barely changes the total caffeine per bean. Any difference in a brewed cup comes mainly from the dose and brewing method used.

faq.question: Why do some people find light roasts sour or unpleasant?
faq.answer: Light roasts retain more organic acids, which can taste sour if the coffee is under-extracted or brewed with water that is not hot enough. Proper brewing technique brings out sweetness that balances the acidity.
